messages:
maria: Heads-up — during this morning's private rollout we saw ~4% of VPC nodes still serving old config after the canary hit 20%. Logs show control-plane acks, but agents report a different config version. Anyone seen this pattern before?

aj: Yep. We've seen propagation windows where control-plane reports success but the agent didn't apply due to a transient mount error. Usually shows up as a checksum mismatch on the node.

maria: attaching the snippet from the node logs:

```
2026-03-17T09:12:21Z agent: received config v3.2.1
2026-03-17T09:12:21Z agent: verifying checksum 0x5a4f
2026-03-17T09:12:22Z agent: apply error: /mnt/config read-only
2026-03-17T09:12:30Z agent: heartbeat -> control-plane (applied: v3.1.9)
```

sasha: Oof. That explains the drift. From SRE side I'd prefer we don't let traffic splitting assume 100% of nodes are updated. We should gate ramps on an observable propagation metric not just control-plane success.

aj: Agreed. Proposal: add a per-VPC "propagation status" that counts agent-confirmed versions. New rollout API would accept policy fields: `min_propagation_percent` and `stale_guard_timeout`. If confirmed percent < policy threshold, pause ramp and notify. Example:

```
rolling_policy:
  canary:
    initial: 5
    step: 15
    min_propagation_percent: 95
    stale_guard_timeout: 10m
```

kevin: For private / air-gapped installs we can't always rely on immediate agent heartbeats. Two ideas: 1) require agents to perform local preflight (validate write access) before attempting apply and post an 'applied' signed manifest; 2) have control-plane keep a signed manifest digest map so any mismatch is detectable offline.

maria: Both sound sensible. For UX: the console rollout page needs a new column showing "propagation coverage" per VPC, with a hover tooltip listing failing nodes and common error classes (:mount-failure:, :version-mismatch:).

aj: Also recommend adding a short-circuit to routing: if < threshold, route canary traffic only to nodes reporting the new version (basically source-of-truth is agent-reported). That avoids sending A/B traffic to stale nodes.

sasha: We'll need telemetry counters: `nodes_reporting_expected_config{vpc,deploy}` and an alert when it drops below X for >Y minutes. Suggest playing with 90/5m as initial.

kevin: Caveat on air-gapped: signing solves tamper and helps offline checks but adds ops complexity. We should surface the requirement in the private deployment docs and make signing optional but recommended.

maria: question for infra: do we have idempotent reapply behavior if a node fails to apply due to mount error? I want automatic retries but not infinite loops that keep toggling A/B caches.

aj: There is a retry loop but it's naive right now. Plan: exponential backoff + bounded retry count + post-failure quarantine flag that requires manual clearance or a successful preflight. This prevents thrash.

maria: nice. Can we also add a debug endpoint on the agent to dump last-apply stacktrace for support? saves us a roundtrip.

kevin: yes — `GET /_internal/last_apply` returning signed JSON. We'll gate on auth.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout job 2026-03-17T08:50:12 completed: canary->20%, notes=partial-propagation, action=paused (auto)

maria: thanks. Next steps: (1) aj/infra to add `min_propagation_percent` and `stale_guard_timeout` to rollout API; (2) sasha to add telemetry + alert rule; (3) kevin to prototype manifest signing + agent preflight; (4) product/console to add propagation coverage UI. I'll track in the rollout epic and we can sync tomorrow. :thumbsup:
